{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AsCp6ExGhourVLzPR9fz4B","type":"tool_result","content":"# League handbook\n\n## The job\n\nThis is a simulated Twenty20 cricket league with ten teams. You have three seasons of ball-by-ball history in `league/` and a list of\nfixtures for the coming season with the announced line-ups. For every fixture, give the probability that the home side wins.\n\nYou deliver a program. It is run on this league and on other leagues of the same kind that you have not seen, so it has to learn\neverything it needs from the league folder it is given.\n\n    python solution/forecast.py --league <folder> --out <file.csv>\n\nThe output file has two columns, `fixture` and `p_home`, with exactly one row per fixture in `<folder>/fixtures.csv`, no extra or duplicate fixture IDs, and finite probabilities in [0, 1]. Row order does not matter.\n\n## How a forecast is graded\n\nThe league is simulated, so the task author can estimate each fixture's home-win probability using the hidden state. The stored estimates use\n100,000 simulations per batting order. They have Monte Carlo error, but are fixed before grading: no new match result is sampled to score your program.\n\nFor a fixture with true probability `p` and forecast `q`, the penalty is `p*ln(p/q) + (1-p)*ln((1-p)/(1-q))`. It is zero when `q = p` and\ngrows quickly when a forecast is confident and wrong. Forecasts are clipped to [0.002, 0.998]. Your regret on a league is the\naverage penalty over its fixtures.\n\nYour regret is compared with that of a reference forecaster. At runtime the reference reads the same public files and engine you have. Its design\nuses prior scales informed by the generating spreads; it is therefore a designer-informed benchmark, not a claim of equal prior information.\nIt simulates each fixture 4,000 times per batting order. Your program is run on this league and on seven leagues you have not seen. You pass\nif your regret, summed over all eight leagues, is at most 10 percent above the reference's sum, and the same holds for the seven\nunseen leagues on their own. Simulation noise in your own forecasts counts against you, so play each fixture enough times.\n\nFor orientation, summed over leagues like these a coin flip (0.5 everywhere) has a little under twice the reference's regret. On a single\nleague anything can happen. Some leagues have little to predict, and there the reference itself can be close to the coin flip.\n\n## The files in a league folder\n\n| file | one row per | columns |\n|---|---|---|\n| `balls.csv` | legal ball | `season, match, innings, over, ball, batting_team, bowling_team, venue, batter, bowler, outcome, extra, position, wickets_before, runs_before, target` |\n| `matches.csv` | match | `season, match, week, home, away, venue, toss_winner, batted_first, first_total, second_total, winner` |\n| `lineups.csv` | player in a past match | `match, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n| `players.csv` | player | `player, role, hand, bowling_style` |\n| `venues.csv` | venue | `venue, home_team, pitch` |\n| `fixtures.csv` | fixture to forecast | `fixture, season, home, away, venue` |\n| `fixture_lineups.csv` | player in a fixture | `fixture, team, batting_slot, player, bowling_slot` |\n\n`outcome` is one of `W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6`. `extra` is 1 when the ball also produced one extra run. `position` is the batter's place in the\norder, from 0. `target` is 0 in the first innings. `bowling_slot` is -1 for players who do not bowl. `engine/league_io.py` reads a folder\ninto the objects the engine uses.\n\n## How a ball works (all of this is public)\n\n`engine/model.py` is the engine, and `engine/public.json` holds its public constants. They are the exact definition; this section\ndescribes them in words.\n\nEvery legal ball has six possible outcomes. Their probabilities come from a sum of effects on the log scale:\n\n1. a profile for the over being bowled (`over_logits`), a shift for the batter's position (`position_vectors`);\n2. the match situation: how many more wickets have fallen than is usual at that over (`wickets_vector`), and in the second innings a\n   constant shift plus the chase pressure, which is the log of the required run rate over the usual rate from that over on, clipped to\n   [-1, 1.2] (`second_innings_vector`, `pressure_vector`, `par_rate`);\n3. the batter's **style** and **quality**, the bowler's **type** and **quality**, and the **conditions**, each a single number that moves\n   the six outcomes along a fixed public direction (`directions`).\n\nOn top of the ball, with a fixed probability one extra run is added (`extras_per_ball`). Batters bat in line-up order. The strike changes\non an odd number of runs and at the end of each over. The five bowlers bowl in rotation, one over each in turn. An innings ends after 120\nlegal balls, ten wickets, or when the target is reached. The toss is a coin flip and the winner always chases. A tied match is settled by\na coin flip.\n\n## What is hidden, and how it is built\n\n* **Batters.** Style does not change. Quality is a fixed talent plus a form component that drifts slowly over months and is pulled back\n  toward zero. A batter's quality can differ a little against pace and against spin. Every player bats, so every player has these values.\n* **Bowlers.** Type is related to the public bowling style and does not change. Quality is talent plus slowly drifting form.\n* **Conditions.** A level for each venue; a league-wide level that moves from season to season and keeps moving; a pitch-on-the-day\n  effect drawn afresh for every match and shared by both innings; dew at some venues, which helps the chase; a small general\n  disadvantage for the side batting second; a lift for batters at their home ground; a personal liking of each batter for each venue;\n  small league-wide effects of batting hand against bowling style and of pitch type on bowling style.\n* There is **no** effect that belongs to one specific batter against one specific bowler.\n* Between seasons about a quarter of the players change teams, and line-ups rotate heavily from match to match.\n\nThe fixtures are played at the start of the next season. Skills are as they stand at that moment, after one more off-season of drift.\n\n## Rules for your program\n\n* Everything it needs must be under `solution/` as ordinary files and directories, with no symbolic links or special files. The entry point is `solution/forecast.py`. It may import `engine`, which the grader\n  supplies unchanged, and `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy` and the Python standard library. Do not change anything under `engine/`.\n* It must give the same output every time it is run on the same folder. Fix your random seeds.\n* It has 12 minutes per league on two CPU cores and must not use the network.\n* The engine is yours to use in any way you like, including to test your own method on leagues you simulate yourself.\n\n## Source\n\nCalibration constants derived from data sourced from Cricsheet (cricsheet.org), licensed under the Open Data Commons Attribution License\n(ODC-BY 1.0). {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WEosyAWSVc9VZ6mhVE8hKz","type":"tool_result","content":"import json\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n# runs scored by each of the six outcomes, in the order W, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6; a wicket scores nothing\nRUNS = np.array([0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6])\n# the two bowling styles, as integers so they can index tables\nPACE, SPIN = 0, 1\n\n@dataclass\nclass PlayerTable:\n    # one entry per player in the league, indexed by player id; these are public facts about a player\n    role: np.ndarray\n    hand: np.ndarray # 0 right, 1 left\n    style: np.ndarray # PACE or SPIN; meaningful only for players who bowl\n\n@dataclass\nclass VenueTable:\n    # one entry per ground, indexed by venue id; also public\n    home_team: np.ndarray\n    pitch: np.ndarray # 0 neutral, 1 helps pace, 2 helps spin\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fixture:\n    # one match's line-ups: the eleven and the five bowlers for each side, plus where and when it is played\n    match: int\n    season: int\n    home: int\n    away: int\n    venue: int\n    home_xi: np.ndarray\n    home_bowlers: np.ndarray\n    away_xi: np.ndarray\n    away_bowlers: np.ndarray\n\n@dataclass\nclass History:\n    # everything an AI agent is allowed to see about the past: every ball, every match, the players, the grounds, the line-ups\n    balls: pd.DataFrame\n    matches: pd.DataFrame\n    players: PlayerTable\n    venues: VenueTable\n    played: list = field(default_factory = list) # the Fixture of every past match (who played, who bowled)\n    seasons: int = 0\n\n@dataclass\nclass BattingCard:\n    # what the innings simulator needs about the eleven batters of one side in one match; built by SkillBook.cards\n    style: np.ndarray        \n    quality: np.ndarray      \n    conditions: np.ndarray   # (11, 5): venue affinity, home lift, hand-by-style and pitch effects for each batter-bowler meeting\n\n@dataclass\nclass BowlingCard:\n    # the same for the five bowlers of the other side\n    kind: np.ndarray\n    quality: np.ndarray\n\nclass BallModel:\n    # Public part of a ball. Holds the measured constants and the five directions; adds up the situation. Nothing hidden lives here.\n    def __init__(self, cal):\n        self.cal = cal\n        d = cal.directions\n        # short names for the five unit vectors: batter style, batter quality, bowler type, bowler quality, conditions\n        self.bs = d[\"bat_style\"]\n        self.bq = d[\"bat_quality\"]\n        self.wt = d[\"bowl_type\"]\n        self.wq = d[\"bowl_quality\"]\n        self.c = d[\"conditions\"]\n\n    def pressure(self, target, runs, ball):\n        # chase pressure, the same formula as in the fit: log of the rate still needed over the rate sides usually maange from here.\n        # `ball` counts legal balls from 0 to 119, so (120 - ball) / 6 is the overs left. Clipped so freak situations do not dominate.\n        need = np.clip(target - runs, 1, None) / ((120 - ball) / 6)\n        return np.clip(np.log(need / self.cal.par_rate[ball // 6]), -1.0, 1.2)\n\n    def situation(self, over, position, wickets, chasing, pressure):\n        \"\"\"\n        The public part of the logits: the over, the batting position and the match situation. Works for one ball or a table of balls.\n        \"\"\"\n        # each term is one effect from the fitted model\n        # np.multiply.outer scales a six-vector by one number per ball\n        cal = self.cal\n        z = cal.over_logits[over] + cal.position_vectors[position] + np.multiply.outer(wickets - cal.typical_wickets[over], cal.wickets_vector)\n        return z + np.multiply.outer(chasing, cal.second_innings_vector) + np.multiply.outer(pressure, cal.pressure_vector)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def shares(z):\n        # six scores become six probabilities; subtracting the row maximum changes nothing and stops exp() overflowing\n        p = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))\n        return p / p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n# Innings Simulator\nclass InningsSimulator:\n    # Plays many copies of one innings at once. Every array below would have one entry per copy, so a ball is one vectorized step.\n    def __init__(self, model):\n        self.model = model\n\n    def play(self, batting, bowling, conditions, n, gen, target = None, log = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Plays n copies of one innings and returns the n totals.\n        `conditions` is a number of one value per copy.\n        \"\"\"\n        m, rows = self.model, np.arange(n)\n        # who is on strike, who is at the other end, and who comes in next, as positions 0 to 10 in batting order\n        striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n        # wickets lost, runs scored, and whether this copy's innings is still going\n        wickets = np.zeros(n, int)\n        runs = np.zeros(n, int)\n        live = np.ones(n, bool)\n        chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n        for ball in range(120):\n            over = ball // 6\n            # five bowlers rotate over by over; posterior we need).\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\nimport scipy.sparse as sp\nfrom scipy.optimize import minimize\nfrom scipy.linalg import cho_factor, cho_solve\n\nD_NAMES = (\"bat_style\", \"bat_quality\", \"bowl_type\", \"bowl_quality\", \"conditions\")\n\n\nclass Block:\n    def __init__(self, name, size, direction, start):\n        self.name, self.size, self.direction, self.start = name, size, direction, start\n        self.stop = start + size\n\n    @property\n    def sl(self):\n        return slice(self.start, self.stop)\n\n\nclass Design:\n    \"\"\"Sparse design: for each direction d a matrix X_d (N x P) so that the coordinate of ball i along d is (X_d theta)_i.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self):\n        self.blocks, self.P = {}, 0\n        self.rows = [[] for _ in range(5)]\n        self.cols = [[] for _ in range(5)]\n        self.vals = [[] for _ in range(5)]\n\n    def add_block(self, name, size, direction):\n        b = Block(name, size, direction, self.P)\n        self.blocks[name] = b\n        self.P += size\n        return b\n\n    def add_entries(self, block, rows, cols, vals=None):\n        rows = np.asarray(rows); cols = np.asarray(cols)\n        vals = np.ones(len(rows)) if vals is None else np.asarray(vals, float)\n        d = block.direction\n        self.rows[d].append(rows); self.cols[d].append(block.start + cols); self.vals[d].append(vals)\n\n    def build(self, N):\n        self.N = N\n        self.X = []\n        for d in range(5):\n            if self.rows[d]:\n                r, c, v = np.concatenate(self.rows[d]), np.concatenate(self.cols[d]), np.concatenate(self.vals[d])\n                X = sp.csr_matrix((v, (r, c)), shape=(N, self.P))\n            else:\n                X = sp.csr_matrix((N, self.P))\n            self.X.append(X)\n        self.XT = [X.T.tocsr() for X in self.X]\n        return self\n\n\ndef ar_covariance(rhos, sd_talent, sd_form):\n    \"\"\"Covariance over K+1 periods of talent + stationary AR(1) form; rhos[k] links period k to k+1.\"\"\"\n    K = len(rhos) + 1\n    R = np.eye(K)\n    for i in range(K):\n        acc = 1.0\n        for j in range(i + 1, K):\n            acc *= rhos[j - 1]\n            R[i, j] = R[j, i] = acc\n    return sd_talent ** 2 * np.ones((K, K)) + sd_form ** 2 * R\n\n\nclass Fitter:\n    def __init__(self, design, public, y, directions):\n        self.des, self.public, self.y = design, public, y\n        self.D = np.array([directions[k] for k in D_NAMES])          # 5 x 6\n        self.onehot = np.eye(6)[y]\n        self.N = len(y)\n\n    # ---- prior ----\n    def set_prior(self, prec_blocks):\n        \"\"\"prec_blocks: dict block name -> precision (scalar for iid, or dense matrix per unit with unit layout (n_units, K) row-major).\"\"\"\n        P = self.des.P\n        rows, cols, vals = [], [], []\n        logdet = 0.0\n        for name, b in self.des.blocks.items():\n            spec = prec_blocks[name]\n            if np.isscalar(spec):\n                idx = np.arange(b.start, b.stop)\n                rows.append(idx); cols.append(idx); vals.append(np.full(b.size, float(spec)))\n                logdet += b.size * np.log(spec)\n            else:\n                Q, n_units = spec  # Q is K x K precision, block laid out unit-major\n                K = Q.shape[0]\n                assert n_units * K == b.size\n                base = b.start + np.arange(n_units)[:, None, None] * K\n                ii, jj = np.meshgrid(np.arange(K), np.arange(K), indexing=\"ij\")\n                rows.append((base + ii[None]).ravel()); cols.append((base + jj[None]).ravel())\n                vals.append(np.tile(Q.ravel(), n_units))\n                logdet += n_units * np.linalg.slogdet(Q)[1]\n        self.Lam = sp.csr_matrix((np.concatenate(vals), (np.concatenate(rows), np.concatenate(cols))), shape=(P, P))\n        self.Lam_logdet = logdet\n\n    # ---- likelihood pieces ----\n    def coords(self, theta):\n        return np.stack([X @ theta for X in self.des.X], axis=1)  # N x 5\n\n    def probs(self, theta):\n        z = self.public + self.coords(theta) @ self.D\n        z -= z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        p = np.exp(z)\n        p /= p.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        return p\n\n    def objective(self, theta):\n        p = self.probs(theta)\n        ll = np.log(p[np.arange(self.N), self.y] + 1e-300).sum()\n        Lt = self.Lam @ theta\n        f = -ll + 0.5 * theta @ Lt\n        g = (self.onehot - p) @ self.D.T          # N x 5\n        grad = -sum(self.des.XT[d] @ g[:, d] for d in range(5)) + Lt\n        return f, grad\n\n    def loglik(self, theta):\n        p = self.probs(theta)\n        return np.log(p[np.arange(self.N), self.y] + 1e-300).sum()\n\n    def hessian_ll(self, theta):\n        \"\"\"Negative Hessian of the log-likelihood (dense P x P).\"\"\"\n        p = self.probs(theta)\n        # per ball 5x5: D (diag p - p p^T) D^T\n        DP = p[:, None, :] * self.D[None, :, :]                  # N x 5 x 6  (D_dk p_k)\n        M = np.einsum(\"nik,njk->nij\", DP, self.D[None, :, :].repeat(1, 0)) if False else None\n        M = np.einsum(\"ndk,ek->nde\", DP, self.D) - np.einsum(\"nd,ne->nde\", DP.sum(2), DP.sum(2))\n        P = self.des.P\n        H = np.zeros((P, P))\n        for d in range(5):\n            if self.des.X[d].nnz == 0:\n                continue\n            for e in range(d, 5):\n                if self.des.X[e].nnz == 0:\n                    continue\n                w = M[:, d, e]\n                blk = (self.des.XT[d] @ sp.diags(w) @ self.des.X[e]).toarray()\n                if d == e:\n                    H += blk\n                else:\n                    H += blk + blk.T\n        return H\n\n    # ---- fitting ----\n    def fit_lbfgs(self, theta0=None, maxiter=2000, gtol=1e-6):\n        theta0 = np.zeros(self.des.P) if theta0 is None else theta0\n        res = minimize(self.objective, theta0, jac=True, method=\"L-BFGS-B\", options=dict(maxiter=maxiter, maxfun=maxiter * 2, gtol=gtol, ftol=1e-12, maxcor=30))\n        return res.x\n\n    def fit_newton(self, theta, iters=6, tol=1e-6):\n        \"\"\"Newton polish with the exact Hessian; returns theta and the Cholesky factor of the posterior precision.\"\"\"\n        Lam = self.Lam.toarray()\n        for _ in range(iters):\n            f, grad = self.objective(theta)\n            A = self.hessian_ll(theta) + Lam\n            c = cho_factor(A, lower=True, check_finite=False)\n            step = cho_solve(c, grad, check_finite=False)\n            # backtracking line search on the objective\n            t = 1.0\n            while True:\n                th_new = theta - t * step\n                f_new, _ = self.objective(th_new)\n                if f_new <= f - 1e-4 * t * grad @ step or t < 1e-4:\n                    break\n                t *= 0.5\n            theta = th_new\n            if np.abs(grad @ step) < tol:\n                break\n        f, grad = self.objective(theta)\n        A = self.hessian_ll(theta) + Lam\n        self.post_chol = cho_factor(A, lower=True, check_finite=False)\n        self.theta = theta\n        return theta\n\n    def evidence(self, theta=None):\n        \"\"\"Laplace approximation of log marginal likelihood (up to a constant).\"\"\"\n        theta = self.theta if theta is None else theta\n        f, _ = self.objective(theta)\n        c, lower = self.post_chol\n        logdet_post = 2 * np.log(np.abs(np.diag(c))).sum()\n        return -f + 0.5 * self.Lam_logdet - 0.5 * logdet_post\n\n    def posterior_cov_diag(self):\n        c, lower = self.post_chol\n        Linv = np.linalg.inv(np.tril(c)) if lower else np.linalg.inv(np.triu(c)).T\n        return (Linv ** 2).sum(0)\n\n    def sample(self, n, rng):\n        \"\"\"Draws from the Laplace posterior N(theta, (H+Lam)^-1).\"\"\"\n        c, lower = self.post_chol\n        L = np.tril(c) if lower else np.triu(c).T\n        z = rng.standard_normal((self.des.P, n))\n        return self.theta[:, None] + np.linalg.solve(L.T, z)\nEOF\necho {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfTgku2aSPDNVRwrjVJAT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012365JHZTGm9dmmkhUkf9ej","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > solution/hyper.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Empirical Bayes for the prior scales: EM with the Laplace posterior as the E-step.\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.optimize import minimize\nfrom fitter import ar_covariance\n\nIID = {\"style\": \"sd_style\", \"split\": \"sd_split\", \"kind\": \"sd_kind\", \"venue\": \"sd_venue\", \"chase\": \"sd_chase\",\n       \"day\": \"sd_day\", \"aff\": \"sd_aff\", \"type\": \"sd_type\", \"pitch\": \"sd_pitch\"}\n\n\ndef _ar_mstep(E, n_units, transitions_fn, start, fixed_rho=None):\n    \"\"\"Maximizes n*(-0.5 logdet C) - 0.5 tr(C^-1 E) over (sd_talent, sd_form, rho_w, rho_o).\"\"\"\n    def unpack(x):\n        sdt, sdf = np.exp(x[0]), np.exp(x[1])\n        rw, ro = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x[2])), 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x[3]))\n        return sdt, sdf, rw, ro\n\n    def nll(x):\n        sdt, sdf, rw, ro = unpack(x)\n        C = ar_covariance(transitions_fn(rw, ro), sdt, sdf)\n        try:\n            Ci = np.linalg.inv(C)\n            s, ld = np.linalg.slogdet(C)\n        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:\n            return 1e30\n        if s <= 0:\n            return 1e30\n        return 0.5 * n_units * ld + 0.5 * np.sum(Ci * E)\n\n    x0 = np.array([np.log(start[0]), np.log(start[1]), np.log(start[2] / (1 - start[2])), np.log(start[3] / (1 - start[3]))])\n    res = minimize(nll, x0, method=\"Nelder-Mead\", options=dict(xatol=1e-4, fatol=1e-6, maxiter=4000))\n    return unpack(res.x)\n\n\ndef em_step(spec, C, theta, update=None, verbose=False):\n    \"\"\"One M-step given posterior covariance C and mode theta. Returns new hyper dict.\"\"\"\n    h = dict(spec.h)\n    des = spec.des\n    diag = np.diag(C)\n    update = set(update) if update is not None else set(IID.values()) | {\"ar_bat\", \"ar_bowl\", \"sd_era\"}\n    for name, key in IID.items():\n        if key not in update:\n            continue\n        b = des.blocks[name]\n        s2 = (theta[b.sl] ** 2 + diag[b.sl]).sum() / b.size\n        h[key] = float(np.sqrt(s2))\n    K1 = spec.K + 1\n    for name, key, keys in ((\"q\", \"ar_bat\", (\"sd_talent\", \"sd_form\", \"rho_w\", \"rho_o\")), (\"r\", \"ar_bowl\", (\"sd_btalent\", \"sd_bform\", \"rho_bw\", \"rho_bo\"))):\n        if key not in update:\n            continue\n        b = des.blocks[name]\n        n_units = b.size // K1\n        th = theta[b.sl].reshape(n_units, K1)\n        Cb = C[b.sl, b.sl].reshape(n_units, K1, n_units, K1)\n        E = th.T @ th + np.einsum(\"ukul->kl\", Cb)\n        start = tuple(h[k] for k in keys)\n        vals = _ar_mstep(E, n_units, spec.transitions, start)\n        for k, v in zip(keys, vals):\n            h[k] = float(v)\n    if \"sd_era\" in update:\n        b = des.blocks[\"era\"]\n        S1 = b.size\n        C0 = np.array([[min(i, j) + 1 for j in range(S1)] for i in range(S1)], float)\n        E = np.outer(theta[b.sl], theta[b.sl]) + C[b.sl, b.sl]\n        h[\"sd_era\"] = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(np.linalg.inv(C0) * E) / S1))\n    return h\n\n\ndef run_em(spec, iters=15, update=None, verbose=True, theta=None, tol=0.01):\n    F = spec.fitter\n    hist = []\n    for it in range(iters):\n        theta = F.fit(theta)\n        ev = F.evidence()\n        C = F.posterior_cov()\n        h_new = em_step(spec, C, theta, update)\n        rel = max(abs(np.log(h_new[k] / spec.h[k])) for k in h_new if k in spec.h and not k.startswith(\"rho\") and k != \"sd_fixed\")\n        hist.append((ev, dict(spec.h)))\n        if verbose:\n            print(f\"EM {it}: evidence={ev:.2f} maxrel={rel:.3f}\", {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in h_new.items() if k != \"sd_fixed\"}, flush=True)\n        spec.set_hyper(h_new)\n        if rel < tol:\n            break\n    theta = F.fit(theta)\n    return spec.h, theta, hist\nEOF\ncd /app && python - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | tee work/em_real.log\nimport sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/app/solution'); sys.path.insert(0,'/app')\nimport numpy as np, time, json\nfrom prep import LeagueData\nfrom spec import Spec\nfrom hyper import run_em\nL=LeagueData('/app/league'); S=Spec(L)\nt=time.time()\nh, th, hist = run_em(S, iters=25)\nprint('time', time.time()-t)\nprint('final evidence', S.fitter.evidence())\njson.dump(h, open('/app/work/hyper_real.json','w'), indent=1)\nnp.save('/app/work/theta_em.npy', th)\nEOF","description":"Write EM hyperparameter module and run it on the real league"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3270,"cache_read_input_tokens":61655,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3270},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0","uuid":"e691f5f4-4bb6-4a63-ae8d-c6e69b1b9567","timestamp":"2026-09-27T09:12:59.810Z","request_id":"req_011CfTgktVZrj735EJg4BuUZ"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfTgyHorwht2Quy57kfGP","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01NovBSdTX1BF5RkoukjbRAr","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /app/work/synth.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Generate a synthetic league with the same schedule/line-ups as a real one but fresh hidden skills; write true fixture probabilities.\"\"\"\nimport sys, json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport numpy as np, pandas as pd\nsys.path.insert(0, '/app'); sys.path.insert(0, '/app/solution')\nfrom engine.model import SkillBook, InningsSimulator, MatchSimulator, load_public_model, Fixture, History, PACE, SPIN\nfrom engine.league_io import load_league, save_league\n\nTRUE = dict(\n    sd_style=0.30, style_mean=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n    sd_talent=0.28, sd_form=0.12, rho_week=0.97, gap_weeks=20, tal_mean=[0.05, -0.05, -0.15],\n    sd_split=0.05, sd_kind=0.25, kind_mean=[-0.1, 0.25],\n    sd_btalent=0.28, sd_bform=0.12, bq_mean=[0.0, -0.1, 0.0],\n    sd_venue=0.10, sd_era=0.10, sd_dew=0.06, wear=0.05, sd_day=0.12, sd_aff=0.05, sd_type=0.03, sd_pitch=0.03, home_lift=0.07,\n)\n\nWEEKS = 8\n\n\ndef draw_hidden(T, players, venues, n_seasons, rng):\n    P, V = len(players.role), len(venues.pitch)\n    role, style = players.role, players.style\n    h = {}\n    h[\"style\"] = np.array(T[\"style_mean\"])[role] + rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_style\"], P)\n    h[\"talent\"] = np.array(T[\"tal_mean\"])[role] + rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_talent\"], P)\n    h[\"split\"] = rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_split\"], P)\n    h[\"kind\"] = np.array(T[\"kind_mean\"])[style] + rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_kind\"], P)\n    h[\"btalent\"] = np.array(T[\"bq_mean\"])[role] + rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_btalent\"], P)\n    # weekly form paths: index t = season*(WEEKS+gap) + week, generated for all seasons plus the fixture week\n    span = WEEKS + T[\"gap_weeks\"]\n    T_total = n_seasons * span + 1\n    rho, sf, sbf = T[\"rho_week\"], T[\"sd_form\"], T[\"sd_bform\"]\n    f = np.zeros((T_total, P)); g = np.zeros((T_total, P))\n    f[0] = rng.normal(0, sf, P); g[0] = rng.normal(0, sbf, P)\n    for t in range(1, T_total):\n        f[t] = rho * f[t - 1] + np.sqrt(1 - rho ** 2) * rng.normal(0, sf, P)\n        g[t] = rho * g[t - 1] + np.sqrt(1 - rho ** 2) * rng.normal(0, sbf, P)\n    h[\"form\"], h[\"bform\"], h[\"span\"] = f, g, span\n    h[\"venue_level\"] = rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_venue\"], V)\n    h[\"venue_dew\"] = np.abs(rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_dew\"], V))\n    era = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_era\"], n_seasons + 1))\n    h[\"era\"] = era\n    h[\"affinity\"] = rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_aff\"], (P, V))\n    h[\"type_table\"] = rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_type\"], (2, 2))\n    h[\"pitch_table\"] = rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_pitch\"], (2, 3))\n    return h\n\n\ndef book_at(h, T, players, venues, season, week):\n    t = season * h[\"span\"] + week\n    return SkillBook(players, venues, h[\"style\"], h[\"talent\"] + h[\"form\"][t], h[\"split\"], h[\"kind\"], h[\"btalent\"] + h[\"bform\"][t],\n                     h[\"type_table\"], h[\"pitch_table\"], h[\"venue_level\"], h[\"venue_dew\"], h[\"affinity\"], T[\"home_lift\"], h[\"era\"][season], T[\"sd_day\"], T[\"wear\"])\n\n\ndef play_match(sim, book, f, gen, day):\n    \"\"\"Plays one match, returns balls rows and match summary. Toss winner chases.\"\"\"\n    toss = f.home if gen.random() < 0.5 else f.away\n    first = f.away if toss == f.home else f.home\n    second = toss\n    xi = {f.home: f.home_xi, f.away: f.away_xi}; five = {f.home: f.home_bowlers, f.away: f.away_bowlers}\n    rows = []\n    totals = []\n    target = None\n    for inn, (bat, bowl) in enumerate(((first, second), (second, first)), start=1):\n        log = []\n        batting, bowling = book.cards(xi[bat], bat, five[bowl], f.venue)\n        cond = book.shift(f.venue, inn == 2) + day\n        runs = sim.play(batting, bowling, np.array([cond]), 1, gen, target=None if target is None else np.array([target]), log=log)\n        for (ball, striker, who, kind, extra, wk, rb) in log:\n            rows.append((f.season, f.match, inn, ball // 6, ball % 6, bat, bowl, f.venue, int(xi[bat][striker]), int(five[bowl][who]), kind, extra, striker, wk, rb, 0 if target is None else target))\n        totals.append(int(runs[0]))\n        target = totals[0] + 1\n    if totals[1] > totals[0]:\n        winner = second\n    elif totals[1] < totals[0]:\n        winner = first\n    else:\n        winner = first if gen.random() < 0.5 else second\n    return rows, dict(season=f.season, match=f.match, home=f.home, away=f.away, venue=f.venue, toss_winner=toss, batted_first=first, first_total=totals[0], second_total=totals[1], winner=winner)\n\n\ndef generate(src, dst, seed, T=TRUE, n_true=100000):\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    hist, fixtures = load_league(src)\n    # rebuild the played fixtures from lineups.csv\n    lineups = pd.read_csv(Path(src) / \"lineups.csv\")\n    from engine.league_io import _fixtures\n    played = _fixtures(hist.matches.rename(columns={\"match\": \"match\"}), lineups, \"match\")\n    matches = hist.matches\n    model = load_public_model()\n    sim = InningsSimulator(model)\n    n_seasons = hist.seasons\n    h = draw_hidden(T, hist.players, hist.venues, n_seasons, rng)\n    rows, summaries = [], []\n    week_of = dict(zip(matches.match, matches.week))\n    for f in played:\n        book = book_at(h, T, hist.players, hist.venues, f.season, week_of[f.match])\n        day = rng.normal(0, T[\"sd_day\"])\n        r, s = play_match(sim, book, f, rng, day)\n        s[\"week\"] = week_of[f.match]\n        rows += r; summaries.append(s)\n    balls = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=[\"season\", \"match\", \"innings\", \"over\", \"ball\", \"batting_team\", \"bowling_team\", \"venue\", \"batter\", \"bowler\", \"outcome\", \"extra\", \"position\", \"wickets_before\", \"runs_before\", \"target\"])\n    mt = pd.DataFrame(summaries)[[\"season\", \"match\", \"week\", \"home\", \"away\", \"venue\", \"toss_winner\", \"batted_first\", \"first_total\", \"second_total\", \"winner\"]]\n    new_hist = History(balls, mt, hist.players, hist.venues, played, n_seasons)\n    save_league(dst, new_hist, fixtures)\n    # true probabilities at the start of the next season\n    book = book_at(h, T, hist.players, hist.venues, n_seasons, 0)\n    ms = MatchSimulator(model)\n    truth = []\n    for f in fixtures:\n        truth.append((f.match, ms.win_probability(book, f, n_true, rng)))\n    pd.DataFrame(truth, columns=[\"fixture\", \"p_true\"]).to_csv(Path(dst) / \"truth.csv\", index=False)\n    # store hidden state for diagnostics\n    np.savez(Path(dst) / \"hidden.npz\", **{k: v for k, v in h.items() if isinstance(v, np.ndarray)})\n    json.dump(T, open(Path(dst) / \"true_hyper.json\", \"w\"), indent=1)\n    return dst\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    import argparse, time\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument(\"--dst\", required=True); ap.add_argument(\"--seed\", type=int, default=0); ap.add_argument(\"--hyper\", default=None); ap.add_argument(\"--n_true\", type=int, default=100000)\n    a = ap.parse_args()\n    T = dict(TRUE)\n    if a.hyper:\n        T.update(json.load(open(a.hyper)))\n    t = time.time()\n    generate(\"/app/league\", a.dst, a.seed, T, a.n_true)\n    print(\"generated\", a.dst, time.time() - t)\nEOF\ncd /app && python work/synth.py --dst /app/work/synth_test --seed 1 --n_true 20000 && head -3 work/synth_test/balls.csv && cat work/synth_test/truth.csv | head -5 && python - <<'EOF'\nimport pandas as pd\nm=pd.read_csv('/app/work/synth_test/matches.csv'); print(m[['first_total','second_total']].describe()); print((m.winner==m.home).mean())\nEOF","description":"Write synthetic league generator and test it"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3717,"cache_read_input_tokens":64925,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3717},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0","uuid":"15a70dd8-2cf9-4252-ad84-47f403186899","timestamp":"2026-09-27T09:15:55.174Z","request_id":"req_011CfTgyGfQQS9EgCYZrt9rf"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfThCk9VbZwYtbpHbD6wx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018aFYXqG1GLo7sezHUuFQP3","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /app/solution/simulate.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Match simulation with per-copy hidden values, so that posterior draws of the skills can be integrated over.\nMirrors engine.model.InningsSimulator / MatchSimulator exactly, but every card may carry a leading copy axis.\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\n\nRUNS = np.array([0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6])\n\n\ndef play_innings(model, style, quality, conditions, kind, bowl_quality, shift, n, gen, target=None):\n    \"\"\"style (n,11), quality (n,11,5), conditions (n,11,5), kind (n,5), bowl_quality (n,5), shift (n,) innings-wide conditions.\"\"\"\n    m, rows = model, np.arange(n)\n    striker, partner, next_in = np.zeros(n, int), np.ones(n, int), np.full(n, 2)\n    wickets = np.zeros(n, int); runs = np.zeros(n, int); live = np.ones(n, bool)\n    chasing = 0.0 if target is None else 1.0\n    chase_vec = np.full(n, chasing)\n    for ball in range(120):\n        over = ball // 6\n        who = over % 5\n        pressure = 0.0 if target is None else m.pressure(target, runs, ball)\n        z = m.situation(over, striker, wickets, chase_vec, pressure)\n        z = z + np.outer(style[rows, striker], m.bs) + np.outer(quality[rows, striker, who], m.bq)\n        z = z + np.outer(kind[:, who], m.wt) + np.outer(bowl_quality[:, who], m.wq) + np.outer(shift + conditions[rows, striker, who], m.c)\n        p = m.shares(z)\n        kind_out = np.minimum((gen.random(n)[:, None] > p.cumsum(axis=1)).sum(axis=1), 5)\n        extra = (gen.random(n) < m.cal.extras_per_ball) & live\n        out = (kind_out == 0) & live\n        scored = np.where(live & ~out, RUNS[kind_out], 0)\n        runs += scored + extra\n        wickets += out\n        striker = np.where(out, next_in, striker)\n        next_in = next_in + out\n        swap = (scored % 2 == 1) ^ (ball % 6 == 5)\n        striker, partner = np.where(swap, partner, striker), np.where(swap, striker, partner)\n        striker, partner = np.minimum(striker, 10), np.minimum(partner, 10)\n        live &= wickets < 10\n        if target is not None:\n            live &= runs < target\n    return runs\n\n\ndef expand(cards, idx):\n    return {k: v[idx] for k, v in cards.items()}\n\n\ndef win_probability(model, sides, shift_first, shift_chase, fixture, sd_day, n_per_sample, gen):\n    \"\"\"sides: team -> dict of arrays with leading sample axis S. Each sample is replicated n_per_sample times. Returns P(home wins).\"\"\"\n    f = fixture\n    S = shift_first.shape[0]\n    n = S * n_per_sample\n    idx = np.repeat(np.arange(S), n_per_sample)\n    home, away = expand(sides[f.home], idx), expand(sides[f.away], idx)\n    sf, sc = shift_first[idx], shift_chase[idx]\n    total = 0.0\n    for first, second in ((home, away), (away, home)):\n        day = gen.normal(0.0, sd_day, n) if sd_day > 0 else np.zeros(n)\n        set_ = play_innings(model, first[\"style\"], first[\"quality\"], first[\"conditions\"], second[\"kind\"], second[\"bowl_quality\"], sf + day, n, gen)\n        chase = play_innings(model, second[\"style\"], second[\"quality\"], second[\"conditions\"], first[\"kind\"], first[\"bowl_quality\"], sc + day, n, gen, target=set_ + 1)\n        second_wins = (chase > set_).mean() + 0.5 * (chase == set_).mean()\n        total += 0.5 * (second_wins if second is home else 1 - second_wins)\n    return float(total)\nEOF\ncat /tmp/claude-0/-app/db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0/tasks/broxur14k.output; tail -3 /tmp/claude-0/-app/db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0/tasks/bngvao2fk.output | cut -c1-300","description":"Write per-copy simulator and check background tasks"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4037,"cache_read_input_tokens":73362,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4037},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0","uuid":"b28e8083-f347-416c-8989-262ecc2c23f5","timestamp":"2026-09-27T09:18:52.545Z","request_id":"req_011CfThCixK9tXCEqE9tDgmW"}

then simulate each fixture many times with the engine's rules, integrating over posterior\ndraws of the hidden values.\"\"\"\nimport os\nos.environ.setdefault(\"OMP_NUM_THREADS\", \"2\")\nos.environ.setdefault(\"OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS\", \"2\")\nos.environ.setdefault(\"MKL_NUM_THREADS\", \"2\")\nimport sys, json, time, argparse\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nHERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\nsys.path.insert(0, str(HERE)); sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent))\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom prep import LeagueData\nfrom spec import Spec\nfrom hyper import run_em\nfrom simulate import win_probability\n\nSEED = 20260927\n\n\ndef forecast(folder, out, n_samples=48, n_per_sample=500, em_iters=0, verbose=True):\n    t0 = time.time()\n    L = LeagueData(folder)\n    hyper = json.load(open(HERE / \"hyper.json\"))\n    S = Spec(L, hyper=hyper)\n    theta = None\n    if em_iters > 0:\n        _, theta, _ = run_em(S, iters=em_iters, verbose=verbose)\n    F = S.fitter\n    theta = F.fit(theta)\n    if verbose:\n        print(f\"fit done {time.time() - t0:.1f}s evidence={F.evidence():.2f}\", flush=True)\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n    draws = F.sample(n_samples, rng).T if n_samples > 0 else theta[None, :]      # S x P\n    rows = []\n    for f in L.fixtures:\n        sides, sf, sc = S.cards(draws, f)\n        p = win_probability(L.model, sides, sf, sc, f, S.h[\"sd_day\"], n_per_sample, rng)\n        rows.append((f.match, min(max(p, 0.002), 0.998)))\n        if verbose:\n            print(f\"fixture {f.match}: p_home={p:.3f}  ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)\", flush=True)\n    pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=[\"fixture\", \"p_home\"]).to_csv(out, index=False)\n    return rows\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--league\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--samples\", type=int, default=48)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--per_sample\", type=int, default=500)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--em\", type=int, default=0)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--quiet\", action=\"store_true\")\n    a = ap.parse_args()\n    forecast(a.league, a.out, a.samples, a.per_sample, a.em, not a.quiet)\nEOF\nsleep 60; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfTive3vsuuKvW5YamEST","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01X7KhGbFXhqNVz8Ec8uBtNT","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /app; python - <<'EOF'\nsrc=open('solution/fitter.py').read()\nold='''    def sample(self, n, rng):\n        \"\"\"Draws from the Laplace posterior N(theta, (H+Lam)^-1).\"\"\"\n        c, lower = self.post_chol\n        L = np.tril(c) if lower else np.triu(c).T\n        z = rng.standard_normal((self.des.P, n))\n        return self.theta[:, None] + np.linalg.solve(L.T, z)'''\nnew='''    def sample(self, n, rng, antithetic=True):\n        \"\"\"Draws from the Laplace posterior N(theta, (H+Lam)^-1), as antithetic pairs when asked. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfTkLAk9g1YNv3Um9zEzV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Pu5STgutLFBY8Kz7jPzzF6","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/logs/agent/sessions/projects/-app/memory/t20-forecast-project.md","content":"---\nname: t20-forecast-project\ndescription: Context for the simulated T20 league forecasting task in /app (solution layout, validation setup, key empirical findings)\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nTask (started 2026-09-27): build `/app/solution/forecast.py` forecasting home-win probabilities for a simulated T20 league; graded by KL regret vs true Monte Carlo probabilities against a reference forecaster (must be within 10% summed over 8 leagues).\n\nSolution design: penalized multinomial fit of all hidden ball effects (sparse design per public direction, AR(1)-around-talent prior over half-season periods incl. one future period), empirical-Bayes prior scales by EM with Laplace posterior, then simulation over posterior draws with a per-copy copy of the engine's innings simulator.\n\nValidation harness lives in `/app/work/` (synth.py generates synthetic leagues reusing the real schedule/line-ups with truth.csv; run_eval.sh + evaluate.py compute regret).\n\n**Why:** hyperparameters matter a lot (fixed wrong scales cost +60% regret on one synthetic league); runtime EM matched oracle scales within noise. Posterior averaging with few draws (48) is noisy (up to 13% regret swings); MAP plug-in and many antithetic draws perform the same.\n\n**How to apply:** if revisiting, keep runtime EM with fixed iteration count (determinism), many antithetic posterior draws, and limit concurrent experiment processes to ~4 (15 GB RAM; runs were OOM-killed at 8).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1620,"cache_read_input_tokens":145672,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1620},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0","uuid":"1b4d3215-cb53-484a-bcca-68c6cc4ee853","timestamp":"2026-09-27T09:59:19.259Z","request_id":"req_011CfTkLA3yK95G5mhPpTED4"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CfTnU9VCFV4uuEU9yWTAP","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The forecaster is complete and verified. The final run on the real league takes 3m15s on two threads, well inside the 12-minute limit, and its output passes all format checks.\n\n**What `/app/solution/forecast.py` does**\n\n- **Reconstructs every hidden effect** of the public ball model by penalized multinomial regression over all ~63,000 recorded balls. Each ball's logits are the public situation plus scalar effects along the five public directions, so batter style and quality, pace/spin split, bowler type and quality, venue level, season level, per-venue dew, per-match pitch, batter-venue affinity, home lift, and the hand/style and pitch/style tables are all parameters of one sparse design (about 4,250 in total).\n- **Models form drift** with an AR(1)-around-talent prior over half-season periods, including one unobserved period for the fixtures, so the off-season decay of form is estimated and applied automatically.\n- **Learns the prior scales per league** by empirical Bayes: EM with a Laplace posterior, 40 fixed iterations for determinism. This mattered most: on one synthetic league, wrong fixed scales cost 60% extra regret, while runtime EM stayed within noise of the true scales.\n- **Simulates each fixture** with a per-copy re-implementation of the engine's rules, 960 antithetic posterior draws × 50 copies per batting order, integrating over skill uncertainty.\n\n**Validation** (harness in `/app/work/`, synthetic leagues reusing the real schedule with known truth):\n\n| league set | EM regret vs oracle-scale regret |\n|---|---|\n| 7 synthetic leagues, per league | between -9% and +2% |\n| pooled calibration slope (logit truth vs forecast) | 0.97 |\n\nTwo runs on the same folder produced identical output. Everything lives under `solution/` as plain files with no symlinks, and `engine/` is untouched.\n\nOne caveat: the reference forecaster's exact design is unknown, so I could only benchmark against a forecaster using the true generating scales in my synthetic worlds. Against that benchmark the program is at parity."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1604,"cache_read_input_tokens":168182,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1604},"output_tokens":687,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db20f289-d01a-4bcd-aa1d-ff3f404648d0","uuid":"17c795cc-49c9-4024-a66c-08ee1e1aa36b","timestamp":"2026-09-27T10:27:20.910Z","request_id":"req_011CfTnU7dKryUmkcwHB7YF3"}
